subject: Renewal planning — capacity smoothing and addendum proposal
messages:
From: Lucia Gomez <lucia@lumosai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumosai.com
Date: 2026-12-15T09:32:00-08:00
Subject: Q4 usage spike + renewal planning

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from our side after the Q4 burst — we saw a sustained 3x spike in inference volume for our notification pipeline (mostly embeddings + short chat requests) over the last 3 weeks. The growth looks sticky: models are being used in new flows across two product teams. Attaching the usage CSV for the last 90 days (summary tab first).

We have an upcoming renewal in mid-Jan and want to understand options for smoothing capacity / commitments. Would Redwood be open to an addendum that:
- increases committed tokens for 2027 by ~20% to cover baseline growth,
- includes a smoothing credit for unpredictable spikes,
- keeps latency SLAs and model mix consistent (we're not changing model families right now).

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync this week to review the numbers? Procurement is cc'd and will need the addendum for review.

Thanks,
Lucia

Attachment: usage-report-q4-2026.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia@lumosai.com>
Cc: procurement@lumosai.com
Date: 2026-12-15T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Q4 usage spike + renewal planning

Thanks Lucia — and congrats on the adoption momentum, that's a great signal.

I'm free Thursday 11:00-11:30 PT or Friday 9:00-9:30 PT for a quick review. I pulled the consumption snapshot and will run a sensitivity model on committed vs. burst credits before the call.

Two quick clarifying questions so I come prepared:
1) Is the 3x spike concentrated on a single route or spread evenly?
2) Do you expect product teams to bring additional traffic (new features) in Q1 or is this organic growth?

If procurement wants to review the proposed template, we can also share a draft addendum (no legal touch yet) during the call.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-16T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Q4 usage spike + renewal planning — prep and proposed numbers

Kim / Sean — forwarding Lucia's email and the CSV. Key asks: +20% committed tokens, smoothing credit for spikes, same SLAs. Drafted a short proposal (attached) and a sensitivity model. Can you review and help decide:

- Proposed commitment: 20% uplift over current annual committed tokens, 12-month addendum aligned to calendar year.
- Smoothing: 120% burst pool (consumable credits) with a 6-month true-up mechanism.
- Economics: effective blended rate target ~4% discount vs current list (accounting for smoothing credits).

Attachments included: proposed-addendum-LumosAI-2027.pdf, run-rate-sensitivity-LumosAI.xlsx

If you both sign off, I'll present to Lucia and run a quick ops feasibility check on the burst pool sizing.

Thanks,
Jonas

Date: 2026-12-27T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Final — addendum draft + next steps

Hi Lucia / procurement team,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Per internal ops and finance review we've attached an updated addendum draft and a two-page cost comparison (committed + 120% burst vs on-demand). Short summary:
- Baseline committed uplift: +20% for 12 months (Jan–Dec 2027).
- Burst pool: up to 120% of baseline per month, consumed then billed at a reduced offset rate; 6-month true-up to handle persistent increases.
- SLA: priority routes are isolated from burst throttling — latency guarantees unchanged.
- Economics: blended rate reduces effective per-token by ~3.8% vs current list for expected mix.

Next steps:
1) If procurement is comfortable, we'll send a DocuSign addendum this week (link below).
2) After signature, ops will provision the burst pool and we will run a 48-hour smoke test on priority routes.
